newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian call money continues soft on good liquidity.
newsitem.headline: Indian call money continues soft on good liquidity.

text.p: Indian call money ended easy on Wednesday in a money market flush with liquidity with closing quotes in the 0.10-0.50 percent range, dealers said.
Call money had opened the day in the 0.25-0.75 percent range, they said.

"The market is flush with funds," said a dealer at a state-run bank. "Even after increased investments in government securities and new bonds issued by financial institutions, banks seem to be in a comfortable position."
Dealers said secondary market trade in government securities was brisk.
"Prices were slightly firm today," said a dealer at a foreign bank. "With call easy, banks continue to be active buyers of short-dated securities."
The 13.50 percent 1997 government of India stock traded on Wednesday at 103.10 rupees against its last traded price of 102.95, dealers said.
The 13.50 percent 1998 stock was traded at 103.20 rupees against 102.99.
Dealers said three-month commercial paper issued by top-rated firms was quoted in the 11.50-11.85 percent range in privat placements.

Financial insitutions were offering around 13.75 percent for one-year certificates of deposit (CDs) while private banks were quoting between 12.50 and 13.0 percent for three-month CDs, a dealer at a state-run bank said. -- Bombay newsroom +91-22-265 9000
